title: Streamed JSON gating and strict parser fuzz experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run an experiment and test harness that validates behavior of the streaming path under strict JSON-mode enforcement and when constrained decoders must recover from partial/malformed fragments, interleaved tool calls, and synthetic corruption. Unlike previous work that focused on batch-mode contract checks, this ticket targets the continuous streaming case where parsers must assemble fragments, apply schema gates, and fall back to recovery strategies with minimal latency impact. Goals: 1) build a corpus generator that produces interleaved tool-call patterns and truncated tokens; 2) run fuzz campaigns against both the constrained decoder and the permissive fallback; 3) measure parse success, time-to-recover, and downstream schema adherence; 4) propose gating thresholds and rollout/rollback criteria for production streaming API. This experiment will also exercise the compatibility layer that maps legacy toolcall wrappers to the new strict serializer and will log the tradeoffs between strictness and customer-visible degrades.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible fuzz harness that can simulate 50k streaming sessions with interleaved toolcalls and truncation patterns
Parse-success-rate >= 99.5% when applying the proposed recovery policy (strict mode + one-step fallback)
Measured median additional latency due to gating < 15ms at P95 under our 200rps emulated load
A documented roll-forward/rollback runbook and an RFC summarizing tradeoffs and recommended defaults
PR(s) merged that add the harness and two unit test suites to CI; dashboards show the three core metrics (parse success, recovery rate, latency delta)
steps: Design mutation grammar: tool-call interleave, truncated token, repeated sentinel, missing commas, extra whitespace
Implement harness that streams tokens into the production parser via test client and records events
Run baseline against current permissive decoder and constrained decoder with recovery enabled
Tune recovery heuristics (prefix reassembly window, sentinel backoff, soft-reject thresholds)
Create dashboard and wire events to observability pipeline
Draft RFC and rollout notes, collect security and UX feedback
comments: 2025-01-30 — Aisha Patel: Initial design doc posted on Confluence, sketched mutation grammar and test vectors. Suggested we prioritize 'toolcall-at-boundary' cases as they caused most regressions in manual triage.

2025-02-03 — Mateo Garcia: Implemented the harness prototype and wired synthetic clients to the runtime test endpoint. Observed that a naive greedy reassembly solved 78% of truncation cases but added ~40ms at P95.
2025-02-05 — Priya Nair (QA): Ran initial 5k fuzz session sweep. Found a regression where nested tool calls could create ambiguous sentinel pairs; attached reproduction logs to PR 128.
2025-02-07 — Platform Safety review (notes): prefer a one-step soft-fallback to permissive mode rather than automatic acceptance; recommended instrumenting a telemetry flag when fallback occurs.

2025-02-10 — Mateo Garcia: Tuned reassembly window and implemented sentinel backoff heuristic; parse-success-rate improved to 98.9% and P95 latency delta dropped to 12ms under the 200rps load emulation. Pushed new benchmark artifacts to the PR.

2025-02-12 — Aisha Patel: Drafted rollout runbook and postmortem checklist. Next actions: expand corpus to include multilingual tokens, add e2e tests that include function-calling SDK harnesses, and schedule a staged canary for runtime-1.20
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on runtime stream behavior rather than batch output validation to avoid duplicating existing contracts tests.
We will coordinate with SDK teams to ensure client streaming backpressure is represented in the harness.
